done.why: I was standing at the mouth of the maze with the axe as a marker, about to start mapping it, when the world told me I had used all 250 turns. I was not finished: the maze, the hole under the altar, and all the outdoors were still unexplored.

about: A treasure hunt in and under a boarded-up white house. You climb a tree for a jewelled egg, drop through a trap door into caverns, and bring back whatever is valuable to a trophy case that 'expects to be filled.' But this version of the underground is partly drowned and partly caved in: the dam is closed for inspection, two passages end in black still water, the Round Room's exits are choked with rubble, and somebody unseen keeps tidying the rock into neat heaps, clearing crawlways with a pick, and barring the trap door behind you. It is about picking over the remains of a place that someone else is quietly maintaining.

ending.what: I got the egg into the trophy case at turn 20 (the stated goal) and reached 124 of 350 points with egg, painting, coffin, sceptre and platinum bar in the case, but the game did not end and there was plainly much more to do.

moments.note: Climbing the tree and finding the egg right there in the nest, 'scavenged by a childless songbird'.
The main goal was done in 20 turns with a flat 'Done.' No fanfare at all; I had to type 'score' to learn it counted.
The trap door crashing shut and 'you hear someone barring it' the moment I went down. Who?
Killed the troll in a single blow. I expected a fight.
Someone has sorted the cave-in rubble into neat heaps, smallest nearest, 'the way some people tidy a room they have no intention of using.' Great line, and a thread I wanted to pull.
Northeast along the chasm just runs into cold standing water. Not what I expected; this underground is flooded.
The Loud Room echoing everything back ('Bar bar ...') until I guessed 'echo'.
'A draught comes out of it, and so, now and then, does an ant.' The crack in the Damp Cave.
The east passage ends on a ledge over a river: 'without a boat that is as far as this way goes.' No boat anywhere I found.
The railing description practically tells you to tie a rope to it: 'the sort of thing a careful person makes something fast to.'
The crawlway has fresh pick marks and neatly stacked rock. The same tidy somebody again.
The chimney only takes a light and one thing. Fair, but it meant dropping almost everything.
The trap door bars again on my second descent, then on later descents it just stays open with no comment. Inconsistent.
Rope down into the Torch Room with the flaming ivory torch on its pedestal, exactly as the railing promised.
The rope ends five feet above my head and I cannot get back up. A one-way trip with no warning.
The coffin would only come when I had shed nearly everything, 'the torch not least of it'. I wrongly dropped the bell and book too.
'Pray' at the altar put me in the Forest with the coffin in my arms. A genuinely satisfying escape.
'The candles grow shorter.' I realised my only light was burning down and the lantern was in the Egyptian Room.
The chimney refuses me even carrying only the lit candles, while repeating that it needs 'a light to climb by and one thing more'. The message does not match what it accepts.
The candles had already gone out when I tried to snuff them; I got the lantern on with no turns to spare.
'FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.' Very funny way to wall off a region.
Turn cap hit one step into the maze, with the outdoors untouched.

wished: Find or meet whoever is barring the trap door and sorting the rubble; the world kept pointing at them and I never got a glimpse.
Climb back up the rope from the Torch Room, or be warned before the drop that it is one way.
Carry the platinum bar up the chimney with the candles; the chimney's own rule said a light plus one thing, and it would not honour it.
Find a boat for the river beyond the Damp Cave, or any hint where one might be.
Get past the drowned passages northwest of the Deep Canyon and northeast along the chasm; they are described as if something is beyond.
Open the egg; 'neither the tools nor the expertise' suggests a way exists.
Explore the maze and the sighing hole under the altar before the turn cap.
See any of the outdoors beyond the three sides of the house and the one forest path.

lines.line: At the mouth of the passage to the south somebody has sorted the nearest of it into neat heaps, smallest nearest, the way some people tidy a room they have no intention of using.
lines.why: The first hint that someone else lives down here, and the line that made me want to find them.

lines.line: It is the most reassuring thing you have seen in some time.
lines.why: About the railing. It told me what to do with the rope without saying so, and made me laugh.

lines.line: A pebble kicked over the edge is never heard from again. Neither, by the look of it, was whoever kicked the last one.
lines.why: Dry and a little chilling; the chasm felt real after that.

lines.line: It is cold to the touch, and quite silent, which in this room is a distinction.
lines.why: The platinum bar, described in terms of the room I found it in. Clever.

lines.line: Ramses II was buried in it, and has evidently been moved elsewhere since, which the face does not seem to know.
lines.why: The coffin's face not knowing it is empty is the kind of detail that makes examining things worth it.

lines.line: FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.
lines.why: A blocked passage turned into a joke instead of a wall.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: Clear, memorable rule; which is why it stung when the same line was used to refuse me with only the candles.

fun.why: Steady pleasure in finding things and bringing them home, several good puzzles (echo, rope, pray), and a running mystery about the tidy somebody. Lost a point to the chimney refusing the candles and the one-way rope.

engagement.why: I never wanted to stop. Every room had something to examine that rewarded the effort, and there were always two or three threads open: the barred trap door, the flooded passages, the dam, the maze.

difficulty.why: The stated goal fell in 20 turns, the troll died in one hit, and the key puzzles yielded to the obvious try. The hard parts were logistics: light running out, carry limits, and one-way descents, which cost many turns of backtracking but never stuck me outright.

interestingness.why: The changes to the familiar layout (flooding, cave-ins, closed dam, an unseen caretaker) gave a strong sense of a place with a history I was only half seeing. I never learned what it added up to.

prose.why: Nearly every examine returned a line with a point of view and a joke in it, without getting long. The chasm, railing, coffin, bar and crack were all worth reading twice.
